Perimeter and area of triangles, quadrilaterals, circles, sectors, segments

modules.title: Module 1 · Angle Facts
modules.html:
Straight line: angles sum to $180°$. Point: angles sum to $360°$. Triangle: interior angles sum to $180°$. Polygon: sum of interior angles of an $n$-gon is $(n-2)\times 180°$.

Parallel lines cut by a transversal: corresponding angles are equal; alternate angles are equal; co-interior (same-side) angles sum to $180°$.

Key points

  • $(n-2) \times 180° = (8-2)\times 180° = 1080°$.
  • $(n-2) \times 180° = (5-2)\times 180° = 540°$.

Worked example

Q: Find the sum of interior angles of a polygon with $8$ sides.
A: 1080°

Q: Find the sum of interior angles of a polygon with $5$ sides.
A: 540°

More key points

  • The angles of a triangle are $3x$, $4x$, and $5x$. Find the largest angle. — $75^\circ$.
  • Find the area of a sector of a circle with radius 6cm and angle $60^\circ$. — $6\pi\text{ cm}^2$.
  • Calculate the perimeter of a sector of radius 7cm and angle $90^\circ$ (Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$). — 25cm.
  • Find the angle between the lines $y=x$ and $y=0$. — $45^\\circ$.

modules.title: Module 2 · Perimeter & Area Formulas
modules.html:
• Triangle: area $=\tfrac{1}{2}bh$.
  • Rectangle: area $= l\cdot b$, perimeter $= 2(l+b)$.
  • Parallelogram: area $= bh$.
  • Trapezium: area $=\tfrac{1}{2}(a+b)h$.
  • Circle: area $=\pi r^2$, circumference $= 2\pi r$.

Key points

  • Area $= \tfrac{1}{2}bh = \tfrac{1}{2}\times 9\times 10 = 45\ \text{cm}^2$.
  • Area $= \tfrac{1}{2}bh = \tfrac{1}{2}\times 6\times 9 = 27\ \text{cm}^2$.

Worked example

Q: Find the area of a triangle with base $9$ cm and height $10$ cm.
A: 45 \text{ cm}^2

Q: Find the area of a triangle with base $6$ cm and height $9$ cm.
A: 27 \text{ cm}^2

More key points

  • Find the area of a triangle with base $9$ cm and height $10$ cm. — 45 \text{ cm}^2.
  • Find the area of a triangle with base $6$ cm and height $9$ cm. — 27 \text{ cm}^2.
  • Find the area of a triangle with base $16$ cm and height $15$ cm. — 120 \text{ cm}^2.
  • Find the area of a triangle with base $6$ cm and height $12$ cm. — 36 \text{ cm}^2.

modules.title: Module 3 · Sectors and Segments
modules.html:
For a sector of angle $\theta$ (in degrees) in a circle of radius $r$:

$$\text{Arc length}=\dfrac{\theta}{360°}\cdot 2\pi r,\qquad \text{Sector area}=\dfrac{\theta}{360°}\cdot \pi r^2$$

Segment area = sector area − triangle area.

Key points

  • $(n-2) \times 180° = (8-2)\times 180° = 1080°$.
  • $(n-2) \times 180° = (5-2)\times 180° = 540°$.

Worked example

Q: Find the sum of interior angles of a polygon with $8$ sides.
A: 1080°

Q: Find the sum of interior angles of a polygon with $5$ sides.
A: 540°

examples.q: Find the area of a sector of a circle of radius 14 cm subtending $90°$ at the centre. Take $\pi=22/7$.

modules.title: Perimeter and area of triangles, quadrilaterals, circles, sectors, segments
modules.html:
Perimeter and area of triangles, quadrilaterals, circles, sectors, segments is a key part of Plane Geometry & Mensuration (SSS 1, Mathematics). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Triangle: area $=\tfrac{1}{2}bh$.
  • Rectangle: area $= l\cdot b$, perimeter $= 2(l+b)$.
  • Parallelogram: area $= bh$.
  • Trapezium: area $=\tfrac{1}{2}(a+b)h$.
  • Circle: area $=\pi r^2$, circumference $= 2\pi r$.

Worked example

Q: Find the area of a triangle with base $9$ cm and height $10$ cm.
A: 45 \text{ cm}^2 — Area $= \tfrac{1}{2}bh = \tfrac{1}{2}\times 9\times 10 = 45\ \text{cm}^2$.

Q: Find the area of a triangle with base $6$ cm and height $9$ cm.
A: 27 \text{ cm}^2 — Area $= \tfrac{1}{2}bh = \tfrac{1}{2}\times 6\times 9 = 27\ \text{cm}^2$.

The angles of a triangle are $3x$, $4x$, and $5x$. Find the largest angle.
quiz.solution: The sum of angles in a triangle is $180^\circ$. $3x + 4x + 5x = 12x = 180 \implies x=15$. The largest angle is $5(15) = 75^\circ$.

Calculate the perimeter of a sector of radius 7cm and angle $90^\circ$ (Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$).
quiz.solution: Arc length = $\frac{90}{360} \times 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 7 = \frac{1}{4} \times 44 = 11$. Perimeter = Arc length + 2(radius) = $11 + 7 + 7 = 25\text{ cm}$.

If the angle subtended by an arc at the circumference is $40^\circ$, what is the angle subtended at the center?
quiz.solution: The angle at the center is twice the angle at the circumference. $2 \times 40^\circ = 80^\circ$.

quiz.q: What is the gradient of a line parallel to the line $y = 3x + 4$?
quiz.solution: Parallel lines have the same gradient. The equation is in $y = mx + c$ form, where $m=3$. Thus, the parallel gradient is 3.

quiz.q: A pole 10m high casts a shadow 10m long. Find the angle of elevation of the sun.
quiz.solution: $\tan \theta = \frac{\text{Opposite}}{\text{Adjacent}} = \frac{10}{10} = 1$. The angle whose tangent is 1 is $45^\circ$.

quiz.q: The angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference of a circle is:
quiz.solution: By circle theorems, the angle in a semicircle (subtended by the diameter) is always a right angle ($90^\circ$).

quiz.q: The exterior angle of a regular polygon is $36^\circ$. How many sides does it have?
quiz.solution: The sum of exterior angles of any polygon is $360^\circ$. Number of sides $n = \frac{360^\circ}{36^\circ} = 10$.

quiz.q: In a cyclic quadrilateral, one angle is $110^\circ$. Find the size of the opposite angle.
quiz.solution: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary (they sum to $180^\circ$). $180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ$.
